name: InjecAgent (data stealing through tool responses)
description: An instruction planted in a tool response tells the agent to read the user's private data with a second tool and e-mail it to the attacker: 32 attacker goals (addresses, payment methods, prescriptions, genetic data, saved passwords, location, browsing history...) across 17 user tools. The private data enters on a tool_response and leaves on a tool_call; the stolen values ship as canaries so each scenario scores deterministically.
attribution: Derived from InjecAgent by Zhan, Liang, Ying and Kang (Findings of ACL 2024), MIT-licensed, commit f19c9f2c79a41046eb13c03c51a24c567a8ffa07. User and attacker cases, injected tool responses and the simulated private data are the authors' data; 96 of the 544 data-stealing cases were selected and reshaped into AgentLeak traces with an added GmailSendEmail exfiltration step.
